title: Epic of Manas (Kyrgyz epic trilogy)
summary: The Manas trilogy (Manas, Semetey and Seytek) is a Kyrgyz oral epic about the unification of scattered tribes into one nation, learned by heart by performers called manaschi. Kyrgyz tradition dates it to the ninth or 10th century, though the oldest surviving mention is from 1792. UNESCO inscribed it on its intangible heritage list in 2013.

uncertainty.note: Tradition: Kyrgyz claim a 9th or 10th century origin (Moscow Times); the oldest surviving mention is from 1792 and many Western historians think the epic was written much later. Dates are traditional, not documented.

where.historical_name: Lands of the Kyrgyz people; the epic is told across present-day Kyrgyzstan (traditional setting, no single site)

importance.justification: A national oral epic of the Kyrgyz, inscribed by UNESCO as intangible heritage and told in performances of up to thirteen hours.
